tps.bug: getBaseConditions returns top-level OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller that appends further AND conditions changes the SQL precedence and widens the org/team authorization filter.
tps.evidenciaOpus: Conceding the class. The PR removed findMany (the encapsulated consumer) and made getBaseConditions the public fragment API, but it parenthesizes only the combined case: insightsBooking.ts:73 `(${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions})` vs :75 `return authConditions;`, and org/team auth is a top-level OR (:173, :206 `(${acc}) OR (${condition})`). Any caller composing `WHERE ${base} AND ...` leaks the first OR branch, so the returned contract is unsafe even if no caller composes it yet. Severity high rather than critical: it needs a caller to append a predicate, a security weakness under specific conditions.
tps.evidenciaAstra: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:74-75 returns authorization conditions without enclosing parentheses when filters are absent, while lines 173 and 206 produce top-level OR expressions. Appending AND therefore constrains only the second authorization branch, allowing the first branch to bypass the extra predicate; the event-type fragment is already safely grouped when combined at lines 73 and 121.
